title: Investigation resilience manifest for night ops
summary: Practical runbook + lightweight spec to make investigation and triage robust during night shifts. Focus is on minimal-cost probes, prioritized traces, and dashboard slices that are actionable with reduced staffing.
body:
Purpose
This note captures a compact, operational-first plan for 'night ops'—the low-staff windows where we must detect, diagnose, and mitigate inference regressions with minimal human attention. It synthesizes metric definitions, trace-sampling heuristics, and dashboard designs tuned for reduced-contact investigations and cost constraints.

Context and motivation
- Night shifts have lower headcount and often no immediate SRE on-call escalation beyond the primary oncall.
- Inference workloads are bursty (customer regions, batch jobs) and cost of full trace retention or heavy sampling across all tenants is prohibitive overnight.
- We need fast surface area (few panels) that point to high-likelihood root causes and an investigation ladder that a single operator can follow within 15–30 minutes.

Goals (measurable)
- Mean time to initial hypothesis (MTIH): < 15 minutes for top-2 likely causes.
- Median investigator clicks to trace: <= 3 (dashboard -> probe -> trace snapshot).
- Night budget: <= 20% of daily trace and query cost allocated to night sampling (configurable).
- False-positive alert rate during night windows <= 10% of alerts.

Signal set (minimal, prioritized)
1) Night-surface SLOs (micro-SLOs): small, high-actionability SLIs we compute at 1m resolution and retain 72h hot, 30d cold. Examples: request_p99_latency_night_window, kvcache_eviction_rate_night, cold-cache-hit-rate_night.
2) Cost-aware error-rate probe: lightweight counters for client-visible 5xxs, model-fallbacks, and API schema-errors.
3) Session-warmth gauge: percentile of session K/V cache hotness (90p, 50p).
4) Thin trace anchors: when sampling, capture a compact anchor (start event, top-3 spans by time, token delta) instead of full verbose spans unless escalated.

Metric definitions and aliases (short)
- request_p99_latency_night_window: 99th percentile token-emit-to-first-token latency for requests between night-window hours (configurable per region). Unit: milliseconds. Aggregation: histogram -> p99 computed across 1m buckets.
- kvcache_eviction_rate_night: number of eviction events / total active sessions per minute. Unit: rate per minute.
- fallback_model_rate_night: number of requests that returned fallback model variant / total requests. Unit: fraction.
- client_visible_errors_night: sum(5xx_count + invalid_request_count) per minute.

Tracing and sampling strategy
- Adaptive budgeted sampler: allocate a fixed token-budget for full traces during the night window. Default allocation: 70% compact anchors, 30% full traces until budget exhausted.
- Anchor format: trace_id, request_id, top-level span timings, kv-warmth boolean, model-variant tag, error flag, minimal token-level durations (first/last token deltas). Anchors should be indexed for fast lookup in dashboards.
- Escalation sampling rule (promote to full trace): when anchor contains any of {error_flag=true, fallback_model_rate>threshold, p99 latency jump > 2x baseline} OR when operator clicks "Collect full trace" from dashboard.
- Tenant-priority overrides: for customers with active SLA contracts or enterprise debug sessions, increase full-trace share to 60% for their traffic (honor privacy/KMS constraints).

Dashboard composition (compact operator view)
Design principle: single page with 4–6 widgets, each actionable (click -> anchor -> full trace or probe run).
Widgets (order matters):
1) Night surface SLO line: p99 latency + alert band + recent deploy markers. Click opens cohort selector (region, model).
2) Error funnel: stacked area of client_visible_errors, fallback_model_rate, model_runtime_errors. Click to list top 5 request prefixes and sample anchors.
3) KV warmth heatmap: by tenant cohort (top N tenants), shows warmth percentiles and delta vs baseline. Click to open tenant probe page that can run a synthetic warm-start probe.
4) Anchor table (stream): recent anchors (last 30m) with flags (error/fallback/latency). Each row has "promote to full trace" and "run synthetic" actions.
5) Cost meter: night trace budget remaining + estimated minutes until exhaustion at current sampling rate.
6) Quick triage checklist (static widget): runbook steps with links (replay, rollback, canary fallback).

Investigation ladder (operator-friendly)
1) Surface: check SLO and error funnels. Is p99 above threshold? If no, close.
2) Anchor scan: open anchors, sort by error_flag and latency. Promote the most representative anchors to full traces.
3) Tenant pivot: if anchors cluster by tenant, use KV warmth and recent deploy notes; consider tenant-side causes.
4) Resource pivot: if anchors show high model runtime span, check GPU saturations, autoscaler events, scheduling latencies (link to infra panel).
5) Mitigation: run synthetic probe (warm-start) against chosen model and region. If it reproduces, open rollback or scale-up ticket.

Runbook snippets (copyable)
- Synthetic warm-start quick command: ./obs-probes/run-synthetic --model X --region europe-west1 --prompt "kv small warmup" --retries 3 --collect-anchor.
- Promote anchor to full trace: click "promote" -> system queues full trace capture, notify operator when retained.

Alert tuning and noise reduction
- Night alert policy: prefer rate-of-change detection (30m window) over absolute thresholds. Mark transient spikes with ephemeral suppressions if followed by normalization in 10m.
- Alert severity mapping: p99 latency increase -> warning; client_visible_errors doubling -> critical only if confirmed by anchors with error_flag.

Cost controls and telemetry retention
- Night trace budget: configurable per region; default 20% of daily trace spend. Exceeding budget auto-throttles full-trace promotions and switches anchors-only mode.
- Compressed anchor retention: anchors retained 14 days hot, 90 days cold; full traces retained per policy (72h hot, 30d cold).

Operational notes and ownership
- Primary owner: eng-observability (Maya Thompson) — responsible for dashboard pages and sampling config.
- Secondary owner: infra-sre (Diego Alvarez) — responsible for resource panels and autoscaling probes.
- Escalation: if investigation meets any of {widespread tenant impact, repeated model fallbacks, SLA breach likelihood} escalate to oncall-sre and product-triage.

Open questions / action items
- Decide default night window per region (suggestion: 00:00–06:00 local region).
- Instrument anchor schema in tracing pipeline and define compact index fields. (Action: Priya to draft schema by 2026-01-20).
- Build UI affordance for one-click full-trace promotions and track cost impact. (Action: Jonah to prototype by 2026-02-01).

Appendix: quick reference thresholds (provisional)
- p99 latency jump alert: >1.6x baseline over 30m.
- fallback_model_rate threshold: 0.5% absolute increase or >0.1% absolute for enterprise tenants.
- anchor promotion budget: default 30 full traces/hour across all regions during night window.

Notes to self
- Keep dashboards minimal. Operators at night want a single sightline to action. Avoid multi-page workflows.
- Prioritize indexability of anchors: the faster a spinner resolves to a trace, the better the MTIH.
- Revisit thresholds after two month trial and adjust budgets based on cost telemetry.

End of doc.
